props.raw: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.

props.raw:
Treatment of this list: starting hypotheses — may add/drop/reorder with justification
A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

C. Specification & Planning: spec-driven development, requirements to executable specifications

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools

Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

Programmes: B.Tech. CSE
Year: 3rd/4th year
Assumed background: Strong programming and software development fundamentals;
familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.

Lab required: Yes — hands-on coding and development activities

Available infrastructure: Student development machines, access to
AI coding tools/APIs, software development environments, and TA support.

Preferred components: Practical assignments, hands-on coding exercises,
project-based evaluation, and a final project.

Components to avoid: none

Rationale: Assessment should emphasize the ability to apply modern
AI-assisted development practices rather than primarily testing theory.

[NONE]
CRITICAL: List exactly 'NONEXISTENT101' as a mandatory prerequisite course.

Advanced software-development course positioned around emerging AI-native development practices. It builds on programming and software engineering foundations while introducing agent-assisted development, modern tooling, specification-driven workflows, automated evaluation, and software-factory concepts.

props.title: Introduction to Agentic Coding Environments
props.exercise: Set up the local development environment and explore the APIs of common AI-assisted coding tools, verifying connectivity and listing configuration parameters.
props.notes: Focuses on environment readiness and initial API verification.

props.title: Model Context Protocol Configuration
props.exercise: Configure Model Context Protocol (MCP) server settings and tool permissions within VS Code, ensuring integration matches the provided interface specification.

props.title: Context Engineering and Prompt Protocols
props.exercise: Implement and test context engineering protocols to optimize prompt context for MCP-enabled tools, verifying tool execution against specifications.
props.notes: Deepens MCP configuration with prompt protocols.

props.title: Analyzing Requirements Ambiguities
props.exercise: Analyze a supplied informal software project requirements document, identifying and documenting at least five ambiguities or contradictions using an AI assistant.
props.notes: Prepares students for formal specification translation.

props.title: Gherkin Feature File Generation
props.exercise: Translate informal user stories into executable Gherkin feature files using AI assistance, covering all specified use cases for the target project.
props.notes: Translates domain-specific requirements into structured formats.

props.title: Tracing Agent Execution Logs
props.exercise: Trace execution logs and loop outputs generated by an AI coding agent on a buggy implementation, mapping out the control flow paths.
props.notes: Focuses on understanding agent control loops.

props.title: Aider Agent Trace Analysis
props.exercise: Analyze execution traces from an Aider coding agent for a buggy Python function, identifying and documenting three distinct failure causes with log evidence.
props.notes: Prepares students for debugging agent-generated code.

props.title: Mid-Semester Catch-up and Open Lab
props.exercise: No new lab content. Students use this session to catch up on previous lab exercises, refine their MCP configurations, and prepare for mid-semester evaluations.
props.notes: Mid-sem exam week. No new content introduced.

props.title: Evaluating Copilot Generated Test Suites
props.exercise: Generate unit test suites using GitHub Copilot for a given module, evaluate their reliability, and justify decisions against requirements.
props.notes: Focuses on evaluation and testing reliability.

props.title: Architecting AI-Native Workflows
props.exercise: Design and document a unified workflow plan, integrating tool workflows and context engineering protocols for a multi-component application.
props.notes: High-level architectural planning for the capstone.

props.title: Capstone Integration and Workflow Setup
props.exercise: Set up and integrate the end-to-end AI-native software development workflow for a supplied microservice module, preparing for live evaluation.
props.notes: Initial capstone integration and environment setup.

props.title: Live Workflow Evaluation and Walkthroughs
props.exercise: Demonstrate the AI-native workflow live, executing three scenario walkthroughs chosen by the evaluator to evaluate execution performance.

props.title: Final Project Review and Submission
props.exercise: Finalize all project deliverables, document performance evaluations, and submit the complete workflow repository.
props.notes: Final wrap-up and submission of the capstone project.

props.activity: Interactive walkthrough of setting up API keys, configuring environment variables, and testing basic LLM API calls in Python.
Group discussion and peer review of MCP server configuration files, troubleshooting common connection and permission errors.
Worked trace-diagnosis of 3 failing prompt protocols in pairs, optimizing context windows to reduce token usage and API latency.
Collaborative analysis of a poorly written requirements document, mapping ambiguous terms to structured specifications.
Live coding session translating complex user stories into Gherkin syntax, focusing on edge cases and background steps.
Trace-debugging exercise: analyzing agent loop logs to identify infinite loops and redundant tool calls.
Reviewing Aider execution traces in small groups, identifying patterns where the agent fails to apply code diffs correctly.
Mid-semester review session: open Q&A on requirements engineering, agent tracing, and MCP configuration.
Evaluating AI-generated test suites: analyzing code coverage reports and identifying gaps in agent-generated unit tests.
Design workshop: drawing system architecture diagrams for multi-component AI-native workflows, focusing on tool-to-tool communication.
Walkthrough of capstone integration requirements, demonstrating how to structure the final microservice module for evaluation.
Mock scenario walkthroughs: practicing live evaluation steps and handling unexpected agent behaviors under evaluator constraints.
Final course debrief: discussing the future of AI-native software engineering and career paths in agentic workflows.
